claims.claim: Models claiming 32K-token context windows only maintain satisfactory performance at 32K tokens in half of cases.
claims.quote: only half of them can maintain satisfactory performance at the length of 32K

claims.claim: At 32K context length, 10 of 12 models drop below 50% of their short-context baseline performance.
claims.quote: At 32K, for instance, 10 models drop below 50% of their strong short-length baselines

claims.claim: GPT-4o accuracy falls from 99.3% at short context to 69.7% at 32K tokens on NoLiMa.
claims.quote: Even GPT-4o, one of the top-performing exceptions, experiences a reduction from an almost-perfect baseline of 99.3% to 69.7%

claims.claim: Performance peaks when relevant information is at the beginning or end of context and degrades significantly when it is in the middle.
claims.quote: performance is often highest when relevant information occurs at the beginning or end of the input context, and significantly degrades when models must access relevant information in the middle

claims.claim: Most LLMs fail to capture long dependencies even when the entire document fits within their advertised context window.
claims.quote: most LLMs have shockingly bad long context ability and fail to capture long dependencies in the context, even when their context window size is enough to fit the entire document

claims.claim: Nearly all evaluated models show large performance drops as input context length increases across diverse tasks.
claims.quote: almost all models exhibit large performance drops as the context length increases

claims.claim: Adversarial decoy problems increase reasoning token generation by 13x, 46x, and 12x on FreshQA, SQuAD, and MuSR respectively.
Newer reasoning model generations exhibit up to 2.3x more reasoning tokens than previous generations.
claims.quote: newer generations of RLMs, while showing a drastic increase in per-token cost, also exhibit up to a 2.3x increase in reasoning tokens

claims.claim: Models overthink by generating verbose reasoning for simple queries, while fixed token budgets cause underthinking on harder problems.
claims.quote: overthinking, where models generate verbose and tangential reasoning traces even for simple queries... enforcing fixed token budgets... can lead to underthinking

claims.claim: Budget guidance achieves 26% accuracy gain under tight budgets using only 63% of the thinking tokens of full-thinking models.
claims.quote: achieves up to a 26% accuracy gain on the MATH-500 benchmark under tight budgets compared to baseline methods, while maintaining competitive accuracy with only 63% of the thinking tokens

claims.claim: Most large reasoning models overthink on easy questions, producing unnecessarily long chains, and several suffer low efficiency despite high chain-of-thought quality.
claims.quote: most LRMs exhibit overthinking in handling easy questions, generating unnecessarily lengthy reasoning chains. While many LRMs demonstrate high CoT quality, several suffer from low efficiency

claims.claim: Performance declines in longer contexts stem from attention mechanism difficulty when literal matches are absent.
claims.quote: these declines stem from the increased difficulty the attention mechanism faces in longer contexts when literal matches are absent, making it harder to retrieve relevant information

claims.claim: Michelangelo evaluations reveal significant room for improvement in models' ability to synthesize long-context information.
claims.quote: there is significant room for improvement in synthesizing long-context information

claims.claim: Current LLMs' reasoning processes are unnecessarily lengthy and can be compressed by including a token budget in the prompt.
claims.quote: reasoning process of current LLMs is unnecessarily lengthy and it can be compressed by including a reasonable token budget in the prompt

open_questions: How far below advertised context windows do specific small models (1-7B parameters) stay reliable, as most sources evaluate larger models?
Which task types (retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, aggregation, latent structure queries) degrade fastest as context grows, beyond the aggregate results shown?
How do reasoning models' thinking tokens interact with fixed output token budgets — do they hit output limits before input context limits?
What is the effective context length for reasoning models when thinking tokens consume a large fraction of the context window?
Do budget-aware decoding methods (S6, S7, S8, S27) maintain reliability at longer input contexts while constraining thinking tokens?
